speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long it has been there and if you notice any red streaks spreading from the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

The history of a painful ulcer appearing at a site of trauma (ant bite) in a patient with inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's) and uveitis is highly suggestive of Pyoderma Gangrenosum, which requires a clinical diagnosis to avoid unnecessary surgical debridement. Given her history of steroid use for uveitis, we must also rule out an infection, but the systemic background strongly favors this diagnosis.

I will request a wound culture to rule out secondary infection and confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Wound_Culture.
